title: Stopping time and force
target: Explain how a longer stop can reduce average force.
criteria: Keep momentum change fixed in a fair comparison.
Compare force using impulse divided by time.
State why cushioning does not remove momentum change.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: Which comparison isolates the effect of stopping time on average stopping force?
options: Same mass and initial/final velocities; different stopping times.
Different masses, speeds, and stopping times together.
cpa.guide: Holding Δp fixed lets force vary only with duration.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: Two tests use the same ball and initial speed. One stops it; the other rebounds it at its original speed. Are momentum changes equal?
options: No; the rebound has twice the magnitude of momentum change.
No; the stopping test has twice the magnitude.
Yes; initial momentum alone determines Δp.
cpa.guide: Stopping changes mv to 0; reversal changes +mv to −mv.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A package loses 36 kg·m/s of momentum in 0.6 s. What is average stopping-force magnitude?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: For the same momentum change, stopping time increases from 0.2 s to 0.8 s. How does average force magnitude change?
cpa.guide: Duration quadruples, so fixed impulse requires one-quarter the average force.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A cushion stops an object from the same initial velocity as a rigid surface. What can remain the same?
options: Average force must remain the same.
Stopping time must remain the same.
cpa.guide: Equal initial and final momenta mean equal Δp, regardless of time.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Why can a padded catcher’s glove reduce average force when stopping a ball?
options: It guarantees zero force throughout contact.
It lengthens the stopping time for essentially the same momentum change.
cpa.guide: Padding spreads the required impulse over more time.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
